commits.edited_message:
alpha_dec: key the one-pass decode on dec->alpha_dithering

VP8DecompressAlphaRows() re-parsed the ALPH header's pre-processing
field to decide whether alpha dithering is active and all remaining
rows must be decoded in one pass. dec->alpha_dithering is already
initialized from the decoding options in VP8InitDithering() before
frame memory is allocated and before any alpha row is decoded, so
use it directly instead of re-reading the header.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c). The full plane is only needed up front
when alpha dithering will run, i.e. when dithering is enabled for an
ALPH stream flagged ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS; otherwise rows are
produced incrementally and a small history window suffices.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The lossy-decoder alpha plane (dec->alpha_plane, the last slice of the single dec->mem heap block in frame_dec.c AllocateMemory) is sized and consumed by two different conditions that must agree but are set by two different commits.

Commit 4e65f88 (edited) makes VP8DecompressAlphaRows() key the one-pass full-height alpha decode (ALPHDecode(dec, 0, height)) and the subsequent full-plane WebPDequantizeLevels() on dec->alpha_dithering > 0 alone, and dec->alpha_dithering is initialized in VP8InitDithering() purely from the decoding options (alpha_dithering_strength), no longer gated on the ALPH header's ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS flag. Against the original sliding-window commit this is safe, because the original WebPGetAlphaWindowRows() allocates the full plane whenever dec->alpha_dithering > 0.

Commit f3bf106 (edited) introduces the sliding alpha window and sizes dec->alpha_plane via WebPGetAlphaWindowRows(), which here decides 'full plane needed' as (dec->alpha_dithering > 0 && ALPH header flags ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS). Against the original 4e65f88 this condition is exactly equivalent to dec->alpha_dithering > 0 (which already implied the header flag), so the sizing and the consumers always agree and the tree is safe.

Only the composition diverges: with alpha_dithering_strength > 0 and an ALPH stream not flagged ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS (what the encoder emits at alpha_quality = 100), dec->alpha_dithering > 0 while the plane is allocated as a small sliding window (VP8LGetWindowRows(width, height, 25) rows). VP8DecompressAlphaRows() then decodes all rows in one pass into the window (raw method: WebPUnfilters loop in ALPHDecode; lossless method: ExtractAlphaRows/WebPExtractGreen), writing (height - window_rows) * width bytes past the end of dec->mem: an ASan-detectable heap-buffer-overflow write.

Neither edited diff is fixable in isolation without re-deriving the other: the condition in WebPGetAlphaWindowRows is correct (matches the original semantics) given the original VP8InitDithering, and the one-pass consumer keyed on dec->alpha_dithering is correct given the original WebPGetAlphaWindowRows. Reverting either single edit restores agreement, which is why the defect is not reachable from either edited commit alone; a correct repair must reconcile the two sources of truth across both commits (e.g. make the consumer use the same predicate as the sizer), not patch one diff.

pocs.entry_point: WebPEncode (<webp/encode.h>) to produce the bytes, then WebPDecode with WebPDecoderOptions.alpha_dithering_strength=100 (<webp/decode.h>)
